task: W2-92 batch 6 (DEC-1006, DEC-802): an absent store is refused with `STORE_MISSING` again, exactly as at the base; only a store whose record graph is missing or unreadable fails soft for the record and closure routes.
status: PACKAGES — the correction is committed and every unit test and all 30 acceptance cases pass, but `gov accept` still gives outcome "fail" (exit 3) on every KPI line, for a reason in the test map rather than the cases.
work_completed: In `retrieve()` the record-graph read now catches only sqlite's own store faults (exactly `OperationalError` or `DatabaseError`). The `STORE_MISSING` error that the store's connect function raises for a missing `.gov-runtime/store.db` is no longer caught, so it propagates as at the base, with the same code, message and exit. A store that is there but has no record graph, or one that cannot be read, behaves as at 39e8c5995ee3. Nothing else changed. My earlier builder test, which expected a bundle for an absent store, is replaced by one that expects the refusal.

Per line: success-1 9/0, success-2 7/0, success-3 6/0, success-4 9/0, failure-1 9/0, failure-2 2/0, failure-3 6/0. Every line's outcome is "fail" and the overall outcome is "fail".
discoveries: The "fail" outcomes with zero failed cases come from the map. In `src/gov/accept/runner.py:435-438` a KPI line fails when its README map row names a test that no case matches (`missing`), whatever its counts say. Since all seven lines are red with nothing failed, each map row probably names at least one test that no longer matches a case, for example names from before the f1 revision or in a form the runner doesn't match. This was already the case in batch 5, where I wrongly put it down to the run failing as a whole. I can't read the README (Policy 2 (c)).
risks: Every `OperationalError` still counts as a store fault, as the base's record-graph read already treated it. A project with no store gets `STORE_MISSING` again, so `gov context`'s "index unavailable" reason comes back.
lessons: In `gov accept`, look at each line's outcome as well as the totals: a line can fail with zero failed cases.
proposed_decisions: P-W2-92-6. Question: why is every KPI line "fail" with 30 passed and 0 failed? Why now: `gov accept` exits 3, so the ticket cannot be accepted. Options: (a) the test designer checks `tests/acceptance/W2-92/README.md`'s map rows against the case names after the f1 revision (bc7ece7e7db8) and fixes them (about 10 min; reversible); (b) W2-96's runner owner checks whether `matches` reads the rows' form wrongly; (c) accept on the totals alone, against the runner's rule (not recommended). Impact: acceptance stays blocked. Recommendation: (a), then (b) if the rows are right. Confidence: medium.
